statement: The ghostcall description inherited from #93 — "linosorice/ghostcall, ~330 lines, zero deps, pure stdlib, pip-installable" — survives on identity and packaging and fails on dependencies. At commit 56b74fc266cde790ef3d4fc474c1388ee2960d5f the repository exists, is MIT-licensed, is not archived, and does what #93 says it does (detect hallucinated API calls in LLM-generated Python). It is pip-installable: hatchling build, console script `ghostcall`, version 0.1.1, with a release workflow. "Zero deps, pure stdlib" is FALSE of the package, which declares three runtime dependencies — click>=8.0, rich>=13.0, rich-click>=1.7. It is TRUE of the engine: parser.py, checker.py, suggest.py and markdown.py import only ast, importlib, inspect, difflib, dataclasses, typing and re, and total 173 non-blank non-comment lines; all three dependencies are confined to cli.py and output.py (126 SLOC of presentation) which a gate rung does not call. "~330 lines" is not a measurement anyone took: it is ghostcall's own README figure, and src/ measures 381 physical / 303 non-blank non-comment lines. Separately and load-bearing for #123: checker.check() resolves a call by `importlib.import_module` on the target's own import roots, which executes the target's module-level code — so this cannot run host-side under ADR-0005 at any size.

citations.supports_because: The dependency list is the half of the inherited claim that fails, and this is the file that declares it: three runtime dependencies under [project].dependencies, against a claim of zero. It also carries the packaging half that passes — hatchling backend, [project.scripts] entry point, version 0.1.1.

Both engine findings read off this file directly: its imports are stdlib-only (importlib, inspect, dataclasses, typing), and check() calls importlib.import_module on the target's import root, which is what makes host-side execution an ADR-0005 violation rather than a preference.

Names the origin of the "~330 lines" and "stdlib" wording — the project's own prose about the four files that matter. This is what #93 paraphrased, which is why the error is a citation error rather than a measurement error: no one ever counted.

Pins the vendored copy to the upstream commit with a sha256 per file, so the line counts above can be recomputed from the same bytes rather than taken on report — the property ADR-0004 asks for and the one the upstream repository cannot itself guarantee.
The upstream original at the same commit, so the vendored copy can be diffed against its source for as long as the repository exists.

_verification_note: This settles the ADR-0004 gate #125 put in front of any image work on #123, and it settles it as a qualified yes: the tool is real and the engine is installable into a per-repo image with no third-party packages, which is the property the rung actually needed. What it does NOT establish is that ghostcall is the right resolver — this checked the description, not the yield, and the false-positive figure (#125 Count 3) is still unmeasured. Two facts worth carrying forward: the repository is a zero-star personal project last pushed 2026-04-19, which is why the source is vendored here rather than cited by URL alone; and the ~330 figure was inherited from the subject's own README, the exact shape ADR-0004 exists to catch.
_measurement_note: Line counts are over src/ghostcall/*.py at the pinned commit. Physical = `wc -l`; SLOC = lines matching neither ^\s*$ nor ^\s*#, which does not exclude docstrings. Engine = parser + checker + suggest + markdown (93 + 61 + 10 + 9 = 173); presentation = cli + output (63 + 63 = 126); the remaining 4 are __init__ and __main__.
